title: Sam’s Big Sandwich
author: Tadoku Note (original)
summary: おなかがぺこぺこのサムは、冷蔵庫の中身を全部はさんだ巨大サンドイッチを作ります。でも、食べようとすると……。

source.note: Original text written for this app.

paragraphs: It is Saturday. Sam is ten years old, and he is very hungry. His mother and father are out. Sam is at home with his dog, Biscuit.
“I can make lunch,” Sam says. “I can make a sandwich. A big sandwich.”
He opens the fridge. There is cheese. There is ham. There are tomatoes and eggs and a big green lettuce. There is some chicken from last night. There is a jar of pickles.
Sam takes two pieces of bread. He puts some cheese on the bread. Then he puts some ham on the cheese. “Good,” he says. “But it is not big.”
He puts on the chicken. He puts on three tomatoes. He puts on lettuce and pickles. He cooks two eggs and puts them on, too. Then he finds some potato chips and puts them on the eggs. Crunch!
Biscuit sits on the floor. He looks at the sandwich. He does not move. His eyes are very big.
Now the sandwich is very tall. It is taller than the milk bottle. Sam puts the second piece of bread on the top. The sandwich moves a little to the left. Then it moves a little to the right.
“Stop!” Sam says to the sandwich. It stops. Sam smiles. “This is the best sandwich in the world,” he says.
But there is a problem. Sam’s mouth is small, and the sandwich is very, very tall. He opens his mouth wide. He cannot eat it. He tries again. No.
“Maybe I can eat it from the top,” he thinks. He stands on a chair. He opens his mouth. The chair moves, and Sam moves. And the sandwich moves, too.
Down comes the bread. Down come the chips and the eggs. Down come the tomatoes, the pickles, the chicken and the ham. They fall on the floor.
Biscuit is very happy. He eats the ham. He eats the chicken. He eats the cheese. He does not eat the pickles.
Sam sits on the floor. Now he has only one piece of bread and some lettuce. He looks at Biscuit. Biscuit looks at Sam.
Then the door opens. Sam’s mother comes in. She looks at the kitchen. She looks at the floor. She looks at Sam.
His mother laughs. “Clean the floor,” she says, “and I will make lunch. A small lunch.”
That day, Sam eats a small sandwich. It is very good. And Biscuit sleeps all afternoon. He is very full.
